newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-EXPOS MAKE NINE-RUN COMEBACK TO BEAT GIANTS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-EXPOS MAKE NINE-RUN COMEBACK TO BEAT GIANTS.

text.p: David Segui lined an RBI single down the left-field line with one out in the bottom of the ninth inning to cap a nine-run comeback as the Montreal Expos beat the San Francisco Giants 14-13 Friday.
The Expos won their fifth straight and Segui tied a career high with four hits, including a solo home run in the second inning. He scored three runs.
"Everyone was saying we're going to win this game," said Segui. "The attitude in the dugout was that way, even down six or seven runs."
Chris Widger had four hits and five RBI for the Expos, both career highs.

"That's the biggest game I've ever been a part of," said Widger. "Just the excitement on the field and in the dugout, and the feeling that no matter what, we were going to come back. That's what made it so much fun.
"In the end, the win is the biggest thing. I'm glad that I got my hits, I 'm not afraid to tell you that. But to win a game when you're down nine runs, that's the icing on the cake."
Montreal tied the game in the bottom of the eighth when Widger's RBI single to centre scored Vladimir Guerrero from second to knot the game at 13-13.
Ugueth Urbina (2-2) pitched a scoreless ninth to pick up the win. Expos starter Jim Bullinger was tagged for eight runs -- seven earned -- and eight hits in just 2 2/3 innings.
The last time the Giants lost after leading by more than nine runs was on June 15, 1952, in a game against the St. Louis Cardinals at the Polo Grounds in New York.
It was also the biggest comeback in Expos history.
Rod Beck (2-2) took the loss, giving up a run and two hits while retiring just one batter in the ninth.

"You could feel it (the momentum) shifting, it's not as much us feeling it, more like them getting an adrenaline rush from the whole crowd," said Giants manager Dusty Baker. "They felt it, and when things got rolling, they got rolling."
Henry Rodriguez had two hits and scored twice for Montreal while extending to an 11-game hitting streak.
In Chicago, Sammy Sosa went 4-for-4 with a homer and a career-high six RBI and Kevin Foster (4-3) allowed three earned runs over seven innings as the Cubs routed the San Diego Padres 16-7.

Sosa put the Cubs on the board with a sacrifice fly in the first, singled in a run in the second, had a three-run triple in an eight-run third and added a solo homer, his seventh, in the fifth. He had driven in five runs nine previous times.
The Cubs recorded season highs in runs, hits (21), runs in an inning and hits in an inning (8). Chicago has won three of its last four overall and five of its last six at home.
Tim Worrell (2-5) took the loss.
In Cincinnati, Reggie Sanders drove in three runs and Tom Goodwin went 4-for-4 with two runs scored as the Reds snapped a five-game losing streak, 4-2 over the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Mike Morgan (1-4) allowed a run and four hits over seven innings to pick up his first win since last September. He set down the first 15 batters in order. A leadoff double by Eric Anthony in the sixth broke up Morgan's bid for a perfect game.
Jeff Shaw allowed a home run to Mike Piazza in the ninth inning, but notched his fourth save. Chan Ho Park (2-2) gave up four runs and seven hits in five innings.
In Philadelphia, Craig Biggio homered twice and drove in four runs and Brad Ausmus added a three-run shot as the Houston Astros outslugged the Phillies 12-7.

Biggio led off the game with his 100th career homer, off Philadelphia starter Mark Leiter (3-4), igniting a season-high seven-run inning that Ausmus capped with a three-run blast. Biggio added a three-run shot off reliever Mike Mimbs in the second to give Houston an 11-0 lead.
Jeff Bagwell hit his 12th homer of the season for Houston.
In Pittsburgh, Alex Fernandez allowed one run over eight innings and Todd Dunwoody drove in two runs as the Florida Marlins defeated the Pirates 3-1 in Jim Leyland's return.
Leyland managed the Pirates for 11 years, directing them to three N.L. Eastern Division titles. But he resigned last year, frustrated with the franchise's inability to keep its top players.
Mark Johnson went 2-for-3, including a homer, for the Pirates.
In Atlanta, Andruw Jones beat out an infield chopper to score Michael Tucker with the winning run in the bottom of the 13th inning as the Braves edged the St. Louis Cardinals 1-0.
Atlanta used seven pitchers who combined on the 11-hit shutout.
In New York, Larry Walker's league-leading 14th homer in the top of the eighth, a two-run shot, erased a one-run deficit as the Colorado Rockies edged the Mets 2-1.
